# object: # The platform state every rak200 repository is configured to, declared once. `new-repo.sh`
# writes from this file and reads it back; `audit-settings.sh` sweeps the account against it.
# Same idiom as `scaffold/seeds.tsv`: one list, read by the thing that applies it and by the
# thing that grades it, so the two cannot disagree.
# Written because a decision about platform state could be made, written down as made, and never
# applied — with nothing to notice. Two were. `allow_auto_merge` was false in nine of ten
# repositories until `gh pr merge --auto`, the merge command this lifecycle documents, was finally
# run and the platform refused it. `sha_pinning_required` was false in six of six until
# `CONVENTIONS.md` §Security was read against the API by hand. One was found by using the estate
# and the other by auditing prose against reality; neither was found by a mechanism.
# A READ-BACK CANNOT FIND THIS CLASS, and it is the estate's own rule that cannot. Non-negotiable 1
# verifies that the write just made took effect — it is silent on the write nobody made. Every
# field `new-repo.sh` read back corresponded to a write earlier in the same script, so a setting it
# never wrote appeared in neither half and the audit reported a clean run over an incomplete
# configuration. The stronger the read-back looks, the more convincing the omission is.
# A ROW DECLARES WHAT A `GET` MUST RETURN, never the call that gets there. The objects below are
# written with three different methods and one of them takes no body at all, so a declaration of
# results is the only shape a writer and a reader can share.
# Not here, and not by oversight: **rulesets and labels have canonical sources of their own** —
# `rulesets/*.json` in `rak200/.github`, `labels.yml` here — and a copy of them in this file would
# be the duplication it exists to remove. `audit-settings.sh` checks that the rulesets are present
# and active, and nothing compares them field by field.
# object   the path under `repos/<owner>/<name>`, or `.` for the repository object itself
# type     `bool` or `string` — how the value is compared, and how the writer passes it
